<!-- pr-reviewer: 1366f4942ea925b12b839aabf109388f1de330df -->

**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Fresh review of head `1366f4942` (the commit that closes the three findings of the review of `25eca3ba4`). I trial-merged with current `origin/main` (`72890060b`): the merge is clean, no conflicts, no ledgers to resolve. I re-read the five changed files and the decision file, and re-ran the build, the tests, clippy and the law check.

**What looks good**
- The three findings from the earlier review are closed, and the pins pin them: body containment against the real tool profile (`a_body_outside_the_rounded_corner_is_refused`), every seat checked (`every_seat_is_checked_not_only_the_mounted_one`), one source for the derived cutter and the assembly (`an_assembly_with_other_components_is_refused`). Mutations m5-m10 are recorded in the body.
- The refusal error names the cutter body (and the seat), and carries the reason.
- `refs #3646` is right for this partial change. No crate edges, no UI, no ECS, no goldens, no snapshots, no process files, no new dependencies. The test file is next to the code it tests (`crates/tools/src/milling_cutter_tests.rs`).

**Results merged with main** (locally, in a worktree on this head, trial-merged with `origin/main` `72890060b`; a fork PR, so no runner):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 1 step, `tools suites: lib` - ok, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-tools --lib`: 186 passed, 0 failed. The 10 `milling_cutter_tests` pins all pass: `a_face_mill_and_an_end_mill_share_one_insert`, `a_45_degree_face_mill_cuts_its_edge_reach`, `a_round_insert_end_mill_takes_half_its_insert_as_corner`, `the_tool_holds_the_real_cutter`, `the_assembled_face_mill_encloses_holder_and_body`, `a_body_outside_the_rounded_corner_is_refused`, `every_seat_is_checked_not_only_the_mounted_one`, `an_assembly_with_other_components_is_refused`, `seats_that_do_not_take_the_insert_are_refused_by_the_fit_checks`, `degenerate_cutters_are_refused_by_name`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-tools --no-run`: all test targets build.

**Targeted tests (step 5)**
- This is a `tools`-only diff: no post or toolpath changed, so no example catalog suites. The light lane (`cargo xtask gate light`) covers the heavy crates (kernel, motion, app), none of which this diff touches, and I did not get it green in a full run: the release build of the heavy crates timed out at my 10-minute cap in this worktree. The previous collaborator review ran the light lane at `25eca3ba4` (all 11 light tests, 0 failures). The PR is P6, so it gets no heavy step, and I have not recorded one as passed.
- No `<!-- heavy-wave: ... -->` record is present; absence is not a finding.

**Requested before merge**
None. I have no blocking findings on this head.

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
- `KAPR` is not read on a round-insert cutter (`crates/tools/src/milling_cutter.rs:176`). The doc comment says so and the decision file says why. A bad `KAPR` on a round insert is silently ignored. A guard that refuses the cutter would refuse a stated value that is not used; a warning or a named refusal would be kinder, but the law is not broken.
- `check_seats` (`crates/tools/src/milling_cutter_assembly.rs:128`) treats every declared port as the mounted seat turned about the axis. A body whose seats are not copies of one another (a different angle, a different z-rot) is refused. That is a strong law, but it is the law the module states (one shared insert, one tool record), and the decision file records it.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
